trees.name: Birnbaum auf dem Walserfeld
trees.reason: Same failure as the Kaiserbuche, and for the same structural reason: this is a symbolic site repeatedly replanted since at least 1564 (sagen.at; de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birnbaum_auf_dem_Walserfeld), not a single old tree. De.wikipedia's own infobox lists it as an 'ehemaliges Naturdenkmal' (FORMER natural monument): the tree that held that status was planted in 1887 and stood until 2014/2015, then came down and was replaced; a new pear was planted in 2015 with a ceremonial dedication in 2016. The living tree today is roughly 10-11 years old, ordinary in size, ineligible as 'genuinely old' or 'visually spectacular'. The memorial plaque and local legends (tied to the Battle of Walserfeld, 1800, among older sagas) are about the SITE and the recurring planting, not about any one living specimen -- fails the destination test, since what draws a visit is the marker and the story, not a decade-old sapling. Both Austrian candidates in this file share this pattern and neither ships as a tree entry.

trees.name: Breite Föhre
trees.reason: Dead: de.wikipedia says the ~450-year-old black pine died 1988 and was removed 1997; only stump and memorial stone remain (trunk displayed in Museum Niederösterreich). Adjacent 'Neue Breite Föhre' (Naturdenkmal, est. ~200 yrs) and 'Kleine Breite Föhre' stand nearby near 48.0719, 16.2722 on the Anninger: unverified leads, look for them as a separate pass.

trees.name: Kaiserbuche, Haunsberg
trees.reason: Not a collectible tree: the historic beech planted in 1779/1791 to mark Emperor Joseph II's 1779 visit to the Haunsberg fell in a storm in 2004 after 225 years as one of Salzburg's oldest natural monuments (de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaiserbuche_(Haunsberg); meinbezirk.at). Its replacement was destroyed by an act of vandalism in February 2008. A further replacement was planted in summer 2009 and stands today behind a 2-metre fence -- so the current living 'Kaiserbuche' is roughly 17 years old, unremarkable in size, and fenced off from close approach. The site (viewpoint, 1898 memorial chapel, 1779/1957 pyramid) is genuinely a hiking destination, but the LIVING TREE fails the destination test on its own merits: nobody travels for a 17-year-old sapling behind a fence. CAUTION for any future photo pass: the Commons photo 'Alte_Kaiserbuche_1/2.jpg' (Alte = old) almost certainly depicts the pre-2004 original tree that no longer exists, not the current living planting -- do not use it as a photo of an extant tree.

trees.name: Rehberger Kreuz, Hofamt Priel
trees.reason: Not a tree. Checked two of the three Commons file pages (01 and 03) directly: 'Das Rehberger Kreuz' is a wayside CROSS/shrine standing on the Wachaustrasse B3 at the Hofamt Priel/Persenbeug-Gottsdorf municipal boundary (coordinates 48d11'25.81"N 15d5'54.48"E, matching the lead's point), a former execution site of the regional court per one search snippet. Neither photo description, category list, nor structured data mentions any tree at all, species, age or size. This is a famous_trees.py false positive, almost certainly matched on the word 'Kreuz' or the surrounding Commons category rather than any tree content. Blocked as not a collectible tree entry; a future pass should not re-check this same candidate without new evidence a tree is actually involved.

Recorded here rather than silently dropped so a future pass does not re-research it.

trees.name: Mesto de las Rozas
trees.reason: Known dead. This is Montalban de Cordoba's 'Mesto de las Rozas', a Quercus ilex x Quercus suber natural hybrid in the Las Rozas area (Campina Cordobesa), about 7km from the town (approx. municipality centre 37.5477, -4.7430; no tree-level coordinate exists or is needed now). es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesto_de_las_Rozas (fetched directly) states the trunk split and the whole crown fell in a severe storm in summer 1995; only the trunk and a regrowth shoot remain on site. The one photo we hold, File:Elmesto.jpg, is captioned on Commons 'El Mesto de las Rozas. Anos 80' (the tree in the 1980s), i.e. it depicts the tree BEFORE it fell, not a current living specimen; publishing it as a photo of a living tree would misrepresent a historical image as current. The brief's guess that 'Mesto' was an Asturias/Cantabria term was wrong; it is a Cordoba/Andalusia hybrid-oak name and this is a different region entirely from the other three candidates in this batch. Hard rule: never publish a tree known to be dead. This can appear only as historical context inside a story about the region, never as a collectible entry. Verification pass 2026-09-27.

Sources: gotlanduppochner.com/2022/06/18/lojstaeken (2022 blog visit confirms it is still standing as a dead snag, described as completely hollow), guteinfo.com/?id=1800. trees.reason: Stands literally in the central reservation (median strip) of the A58 motorway at Ulvenhout, part of Breda; Dutch name is 'Troeteleik' or 'Anneville-eik', not merely the contest's translated 'Pet oak'. It is not on private land and the contest page's framing as a Dutch Tree of the Year winner (2018/2019) is real, but there is no way to reach the trunk without walking onto an active dual-carriageway highway: no path, verge or safe pedestrian access exists or could exist to a tree standing between the carriageways. Fails the 'publicly accessible' half of the qualifying bar outright, a harder fail than a locked gate. Not a collectible point in any sense this project can offer someone. Separately, and not the reason for blocking: Rijkswaterstaat has planned to fell it for A58 widening since at least 2015 (original target year 2020, per Omroep Brabant 2016-11-28 and ilovebreda.nl 2016-11-29, cost of an alternative viaduct to save it put at over EUR3.5 million); the widening project (InnovA58, Sint-Annabosch-Galder section) has been paused since June 2023 over nitrogen permitting, cost and labour issues per rijkswaterstaat.nl's own project page (fetched 2026-09-25), so the tree is very likely still standing today, but this was never the deciding fact. trees.reason: PRIVATE FACTORY GROUNDS, fails hard rule 10. Multiple independent Bulgarian sources agree this is the plane tree in the yard of the former textile factory "Purvi Mai" (First of May), now owned by Galatex AD (with Asen Nikolov 1 AD), in the Asparuhovo neighbourhood of Varna (novavarna.net, pik.bg). moreto.net states explicitly: "Zashtitenoto darvo e ot ogranichen dostap i ne mozhe svobodno da se razgledа" ("The protected tree has limited access and cannot be freely viewed"). This is a factory yard, not a churchyard, campus or company grounds with an open gate; nothing found suggests a standing public visiting arrangement. Facts otherwise check out and disagree only in the way old-tree measurements always do across retellings: age given as 1045, 1051 and 1054 years depending on the outlet and year of writing (all traced to the same claim of dating to the First Bulgarian Empire, so the exact figure is a moving calculation rather than a documented planting date; contest's own framing, "7th-11th century," is the honest way to state it, not a single year), height 15 or 18m, girth 7.7m or roughly 9m at the base. Protected since March 1969 by Forestry Ministry order; entered in the Regional Inspectorate for Environment and Waters (Varna) old-tree register; local legend that Khan Asparuh rested in its shade. If Galatex/the factory ever documents open visiting hours or a public path reaching the tree, this is worth revisiting. Sources checked: https://old-news.bnr.bg/varna/post/101733036/varnensko-darvo-na-1050-g-s-nominacia-za-darvo-na-godinata , https://www.dnes.bg/a/64-stranata/343385-edno-ot-nay-starite-darveta-u-nas-vav-varna , https://www.moreto.net/novini.php?n=244165 , https://novavarna.net/2023/01/27/ , https://pik.bg/10-vekovni-darveta-se-namirat-na-teritoriyata-na-varna-news906373.html

trees.reason:
PRIVATE PROPERTY, access by the owner's permission rather than a genuinely open or reliably bookable site; fails hard rule 10. This is a real, distinct tree, not either of our two candidates flagged in this record's own earlier note: it stands in the garden of Casa de Margaride (also 'Quinta de Margaride' or the contest's 'Villa Margaridi'), a noble manor house in the Mesao Frio parish of Guimaraes, still owned by descendants of the Counts of Margaride per its own English Wikipedia page ('whose descendants remain owners today'). It is NOT gui_003 (The Camellias of Palacio Vila Flor, a different, municipally-run building, roughly 2.05km from the contest's published pin) and NOT gui_005 (The Oak of Santa Marinha da Costa, 0.92km away per this record's nearest_published field but a different species and a different site entirely). The 0.9km note previously on this record pointing at gui_003 does not hold up: gui_003 is over 2km from the contest coordinate, not 0.9km.

ACCESS: jardinshistoricos.pt (a Portuguese historic-gardens directory) lists it plainly as 'Paid entry / Access by appointment', with a personal email (casademaride@gmail.com) and mobile number as the only contact, not a ticketing platform or published opening hours. A local heritage association (A Muralha, Associacao de Defesa do Patrimonio de Guimaraes) has organised occasional guided visits to the gardens with registration by email (guimaraesmuralha@gmail.com), which reads as a one-off arranged outing rather than a standing, anyone-can-book tour. Per the paid-entry/booking test this project uses (a price and a schedule we can state, versus somebody's permission we cannot promise), this reads as the second: there is no evidence of a fixed, publicly published visiting schedule or ticket, only 'ask the family or a heritage group and see what they can arrange.' The garden's own 'Monument of Public Interest' heritage designation (2012) is a protection status against alteration or demolition, not a public-access requirement, and does not change the ownership.

If this changes (a standing, publicly bookable visiting programme with fixed hours or tickets is documented later), this is worth revisiting: the tree itself checks out. Widely and consistently reported at roughly 300 years old (contest page; Publico, Wilder, Diario do Minho and Agronegocios.eu, all independent Portuguese outlets covering its national Arvore do Ano 2024 win, 3,900 votes nationally before 13,508 and 4th place in the European contest); one source (Portal Agronegocios.eu) gives dimensions of 6.30m in diameter (almost certainly the shaped topiary canopy spread, not a trunk girth, for a camellia grown as ornamental topiary) and 6.15m in height. The estate's garden holds several centuries-old Camellia japonica cultivars (Alba Plena, Variegata, Pompone) reported as unique in Europe, per the Diario do Minho/Camara Municipal coverage of its 2012 heritage classification; unclear from available sources whether the contest tree is one specific named specimen within that collection or the planted group is being treated as one. The 6.30m/6.15m/300-year/3,900-vote figures were confirmed on a direct fetch of agronegocios.eu itself (not taken from a search summary), which also describes the shape as bell-like ('campanula'), consistent with a clipped topiary specimen. Sources: https://www.agronegocios.eu/noticias/camelia-japoneira-vence-7-edicao-nacional-da-arvore-do-ano/ ; https://wilder.pt/historias/camelia-japoneira-de-guimaraes-eleita-a-arvore-do-ano-de-2024 ; https://www.publico.pt/2024/01/10/ciencia/noticia/arvore-portuguesa-2024-cameliajaponeira-raizes-guimaraes-2076357 (403'd automated fetch, used via search summary only for the headline fact that press coverage exists, not for any figure); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_de_Margaride ; https://www.jardinshistoricos.pt/ad/412 ; https://www.cm-guimaraes.pt/noticias/noticia/galardao-de-arvore-portuguesa-do-ano-foi-entregue-a-camelia-de-guimaraes .

trees.name: Haenge-Buchen im Helfenberger Park
trees.note: ND 78, park of Schloss Helfenberg. Weaker entry now; could be written as the survivor if a photograph of it is found.

Alive status doubtful, remote spot. Re-check before any use; Commons category Naturdenkmal Politische Buche im Kleditschgrund has photos.

trees.name: Rotbuche Tännichtstraße (Rochwitz)

trees.name: Alberteiche im Großen Garten
trees.note: Planted 23 Oct 1893 for King Albert's 50th military jubilee, on a low mound at Herkulesallee corner Friedrich-Bouche-Weg south of the Neuteich, part of a tree group, no sign, no size figure.
